chunks: "If you have intercourse with your spouse after binding the ihram but before reciting the talbiyah, then there is nothing upon you. If you have intercourse while you are in ihram before standing at al-Mash'ar, then a camel is upon you, and the hajj must be performed again the following year. If you have intercourse after your standing at al-Mash'ar, then a camel is upon you, but the hajj of the following year is not upon you. And if you were forgetful, inattentive, or ignorant, then there is nothing upon you."

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: the consecrated state entered for hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.الْمَشْعَرِ: al-Mash'ar, the sacred station where the pilgrim stands during hajj
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: a camel offered as sacrificial expiation
key_terms.تُلَبِّيَ: to recite the talbiyah marking the response to the hajj call
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: one who is in the state of ihram
key_terms.نَاسِيًا: forgetful, acting without remembering the ruling or circumstance

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on intercourse during ihram before or after standing at al-Mash'ar?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings regarding intercourse during hajj while in ihram, distinguishing between different stages of the rite. It states that the ruling varies depending on whether talbiyah has been recited and whether standing at al-Mash'ar has occurred, while also exempting the forgetful, inattentive, and ignorant person from liability.
